claim: For every odd prime \(p\) and every \(r\in\{3,5,7\}\), let \(\mathcal B_{r,p}\) be the set of integers \(0\le\beta<p^2\) for which \(\tau(8(p^2n+\beta)+r)\equiv0\pmod4\) for every \(n\ge0\). Put \(c_\beta=8\beta+r\). Then \(\beta\in\mathcal B_{r,p}\) exactly when \(p\mid c_\beta\), \(p^2\nmid c_\beta\), and, with \(t=c_\beta/p\), either \(t\not\equiv1\pmod8\) or \(t\) is a quadratic nonresidue modulo \(p\). Consequently \(|\mathcal B_{r,p}|=(p-1)/2\) when \(p\equiv r\pmod8\), and \(|\mathcal B_{r,p}|=p-1\) otherwise. This proves Conjecture 3 of Merca, Axioms 11 (2022), 342.
integrity: The universal statement is supported by a symbolic proof. Finite computation is used only as a regression check and is not presented as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem settles Conjecture 3 only for \(r\in\{3,5,7\}\), exactly as posed; it does not settle the \(r=1\) problem or the source paper's other conjectures. Literature noncoverage retains the risk of an unindexed or differently phrased prior proof.
title: Merca's Conjecture 3: exact prime-square divisor congruences modulo \(4\)
